articles.title: 'Shouting match from hell': Trump, Netanyahu clash in explosive phone call over Iran war
articles.summary: A war that brought Washington and Tel Aviv together is now exposing a growing divide between their leaders.
articles.body: A war that brought Washington and Tel Aviv together is now exposing a growing divide between their leaders.US President Donald Trump wants to give diplomacy with Iran another chance, but Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for regime change in Tehran and renewed military action. The disagreement comes as Netanyahu faces another battle closer to home, with Israel's opposition moving to form a coalition government that could end his long hold on power.According to a report by Israeli news outlet Ynet, citing sources familiar with the conversation, US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had a heated telephone exchange over the weekend over the next course of action against Iran.One source described the conversation as a "shouting match from hell", highlighting growing differences between the two leaders over whether to resume military strikes against Tehran or pursue a diplomatic settlement.Netanyahu's office rejected the account, calling it "fake news, complete nonsense", while a senior Israeli official denied that the conversation was confrontational.The reported confrontation comes amid Netanyahu's efforts to persuade Trump to resume military operations against Iran. According to the Financial Times, citing a diplomat familiar with the discussions, the Israeli leader has been calling Trump daily to press for renewed strikes, even as officials in Washington and regional leaders seek to prevent another escalation.Trump, however, has signalled that he sees no immediate need for further military action. In an interview with CBS' 60 Minutes, aired on November 8, the US president said he was not looking to escalate the conflict. "Well, I'm not looking to. I don't think there's any reason to," Trump said when asked about the possibility of renewed military action against Iran.Netanyahu, on the other hand, has taken a considerably harder position, arguing that military strikes alone cannot permanently eliminate the threat posed by Tehran. The Israeli leader believes Iran could rebuild its nuclear capabilities under the existing leadership, making regime change essential to Israel's long-term security.Speaking at the swearing-in of Israel's 26th Knesset on November 10, Netanyahu reiterated his demand for regime change in Iran, saying that military strikes alone would not permanently remove the nuclear threat."Iran is working to renew the nuclear threat. The only way to permanently remove this existential threat is by toppling the regime of the ayatollahs," Netanyahu said.He also warned that Israel would face international pressure to accept a nuclear agreement that could allow Iran's current leadership to remain in power. Netanyahu further called for a national unity government in Israel, saying the country needed political unity to deal with growing security challenges.The speech comes as Netanyahu faces an uncertain political future after the October 27 election left his Likud-led bloc with 53 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority.President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government after 67 lawmakers backed his candidature. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to secure a coalition. If successful, Netanyahu will lose the prime minister's office and Likud will move into opposition.You use AI every day. articles.title: 4 personnel killed as military helicopter crashes in southern Turkey
articles.summary: Four military personnel were killed after an S-70 helicopter crashed in southern Turkey on Thursday, the Turkish defence ministry said.
articles.body: Four military personnel were killed after an S-70 helicopter crashed in southern Turkey on Thursday, the Turkish defence ministry said.Television footage showed the wreckage engulfed in flames near a cluster of buildings in an otherwise open area. According to the Demiroren News Agency, the fire spread to a nearby house, but no casualties were reported on the ground.The helicopter crashed in Samankoy, a neighbourhood on the southern outskirts of Malatya, in the early evening. Police, firefighters and medical teams were rushed to the crash site.In a social media post, the ministry confirmed that all four personnel aboard the aircraft were killed and expressed condolences to their families and the Turkish armed forces.The ministry said that the cause of the crash remains unknown.You use AI every day. articles.title: With rain short, Chennai braces for tighter water supply this summer
articles.summary: Chennai faces summer water stress as reservoir storage drops 48% year-on-year and groundwater deepens 1.71m; Metrowater may ration supply, rely on desalination.
articles.body: The city is running low on water, both above and below ground. A poor monsoon so far has left reservoirs with 48% less water than they held at this time last year, while groundwater levels are about 45% deeper.Metrowater is looking to the sky for relief, hoping for more rain until mid-Dec. “If the situation does not improve, we might have to consider rationalising water supply, while relying on desalination plants,” an official said.The city’s five principal reservoirs, Poondi, Cholavaram, Red Hills, Chembarambakkam and Kannankottai-Thervoy Kandigai, held 4.79 thousand Million Cubic Feet (tmcft) on Thursday, compared with 10 tmcft on the same day last year. That is 41% of their combined capacity of 11.75 tmcft. Including Veeranam, storage totals 5.71 tmcft, down from 10.93 tmcft, a drop of nearly 47%.Groundwater levels also dipped. The average depth rose from 3.77m in Oct 2025 to 5.48m in Oct this year, a fall of 1.71m, or 45%. Madhavaram recorded the sharpest fall, from 5.80m to 10.81m, followed by Thiru-Vi-Ka Nagar, where levels dropped from 4.57m to 8.82m. However, levels across the city improved by nearly a metre from last month.Metrowater says desalination will cushion the shortfall. On Wednesday, the 110 million litres a day (mld) and 150mld plants supplied 100mld and 87mld, respectively. By Thursday, the supply rose to more than 100mld in both plants. “Both the Nemmelli plants can be operated at full capacity. By Feb, the Minjur plant, which has a 100mld capacity, will yield at least 20mld,” a senior official said. “We are confident of handling the situation,” he said.However, water experts are not so optimistic. They warn that the situation is worrying and the offered solution is dangerous. “Surplus rain was expected this year. But that has not been the case so far,” said S Janakarajan, a retired professor at the Madras Institute of Development Studies (MIDS).Evaporation from the soil and water lost through plants, together called evapotranspiration, would be very high in summer. “Water extraction will be much higher than groundwater recharge,” he said, hoping the coming cyclones would bring some relief to the reservoirs.Janakarajan said the state govt lacked a water security plan despite several warnings about El Niño. “Chennai receives an average of 120cm of rainfall every year. Desalination plants can never be the solution. It is a lazy way out by the govt and harms the coastal ecosystem,” he said.Sekhar Raghavan, Chennai’s ‘Rain Man’ and founder of The Rain Centre, an NGO, said residents should not wait for the state to supply water. They should recharge groundwater themselves. “By this time, Chennai should have had at least 140 cm of rainfall, but we received only 110 cm as of Nov 10,” he said.The govt must act on two fronts. “First, appoint third-party monitors for rainwater harvesting. In many places, builders have not constructed the systems properly, yet the CMDA approved them,” he said. TVK govt relaunched its rainwater-harvesting initiative. “But enforcement will not improve without outside monitors,” he said.“Second, the govt must draw up a preventive plan before a drought or flood strikes, and it must involve experts with decades of experience,” he said. “Officials and engineers are not enough. The govt must change its attitude and seek outside expertise.”“Both floods and droughts are man-made,” he said. “If govts do not learn from experience, the same problems will recur, and we will keep having the same discussions with no change.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news.
